messages.subject: Running NicheMapR & running NicheMapR inside
parts:
Hi everyone!

I was hoping I might ask some advice on which is the path of least resistance. 

I've got seasonal data of a burrowing ectotherm sp. change in mass after being kept outside and inside (at a fairly consistent temperature) for periods of several weeks, plus the mass of their brood balls.

As some of the features of the microclimate model (including necessary argument longlat) can't be included for accurate results for the inside treatment, am I better off manually overriding specific variables, or making data tables to replicate micro global?

Many thanks,
Alex

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Running NicheMapR & running NicheMapR inside
parts:
Hi Alex,

You can certainly overwrite the microclimate input files with experimental conditions. You could run the micro_global function with default settings to get the data frames, then set the behaviours appropriately (no burrowing or shade seeking, etc.) and replace the local wind speed, local air temperature, local humidity, soil surface and sky temperature in metout and soil to the appropriate ones for your laboratory/indoor conditions.

All the best,
Mike
